stops.summary: A Hydra stretches and contracts with different networks. A box jellyfish can learn near its eyes. In a comb jelly, parts of a nerve net even share one continuous membrane. These are three different solutions to coordinating a body.

structures.description: The box jellyfish has four sensory centers connected to a nerve running around its bell. Each center brings eyes and nearby nerve tissue together.
structures.origin_scope: The observation is documented. The available evidence does not date the origin of this particular feature.

abilities.name: Approach a distant target
abilities.description: Researchers put sound recording tags on trained bottlenose dolphins. Their click timing changed with target distance as they swam toward it.

abilities.name: Switch how clicks are grouped
abilities.description: At longer ranges, the dolphins frequently sent packets of clicks before waiting for returning echoes. Individual animals used different timing strategies.

nuances.claim: Three times as many neurons means three times as many cortical neurons.

nuances.claim: A dolphin must wait for each echo before making another click.
nuances.reality: Free-swimming bottlenose dolphins could group clicks into packets at long range.
nuances.evidence_quote: not a fixed echolocation strategy

stops.summary: The measured adult human brain averages about 86 billion neurons. Regional counts tell a different story from skull volume, the measure fossils preserve. Recordings in living people reveal that individual neurons can respond to different pictures of the same person.

structures.name: Action-responsive motor cortex
structures.description: Some macaque motor-planning neurons fire during both a mouth action and observation of a similar action by another individual.
structures.evidence_quote: execution and observation of mouth actions
structures.origin_scope: Elaboration of inherited mammalian cortex; the first appearance of matching action responses is undated.

structures.name: Identity-sensitive temporal neurons
structures.description: Some human neurons on the inner side of the temporal lobe respond to very different pictures of the same person or landmark.
structures.origin_scope: The observation is documented. The available evidence does not date the origin of this particular feature.

structures.name: Speech-sensitive parietal cortex
structures.description: Researchers recording individual neurons near the side of the human brain found signals related to words participants spoke silently.
structures.evidence_quote: significant neural representation of internal and vocalized speech
structures.origin_scope: Elaboration of inherited mammalian cortex; the experiment does not date silent speech.

abilities.name: Represent observed actions
abilities.description: Macaque recordings identified cells active during eating movements and while watching similar movements. Some also responded when another individual made a mouth gesture.

abilities.name: Recognize identity across images
abilities.description: In recordings from people viewing different images of one individual, some neurons responded across viewpoints and sometimes even to the written name.

abilities.name: Form words silently
abilities.description: In two people doing a limited word task, researchers could predict some silently spoken words from activity in a patch of parietal cortex.
abilities.evidence_quote: internally spoken and vocalized words were significantly decodable

nuances.claim: Human neuron counts break every primate scaling rule.

nuances.evidence_quote: expected for a primate of human proportions

nuances.claim: Modern humans always had larger brains than Neanderthals.
nuances.reality: Estimated skull-cavity volumes overlap. In one comparison, Neanderthals averaged 1,450 milliliters and present-day humans averaged 1,328 milliliters. Fossil skulls preserve a volume estimate, not a neuron count.
nuances.evidence_quote: present-day humans (mean, 1328 ml; SD, 164 ml) and Neandertals (mean, 1450 ml; SD, 189 ml)

diverged_mya.value_basis: Midpoint of the published composite interval in Table 1. This is a branch split, not the age of the living species.

neuron_counts.region: classified neurons across the entire body of one three-day-old larva; excludes developing, unclassified cells
neuron_counts.method: Researchers traced cells in serial electron micrographs and classified them by shape, location and connections.

stops.summary: A swimming ragworm larva has head circuits that steer it toward light, and others that send it down in ultraviolet light. Researchers have traced the connections throughout the body of a three-day-old larva.

structures.name: Larval eyespots
structures.description: Each early eyespot has a light-sensitive cell and a pigment cell that shades it from one side.
structures.evidence_quote: a photoreceptor and a shading pigment cell
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

structures.name: Ultraviolet-sensitive cells
structures.description: Light-sensitive cells of an ancient type sit inside the larval brain. They respond to ultraviolet light and feed into the circuit for swimming toward visible light.
structures.evidence_quote: two main lines of photoreceptor-cell evolution

structures.name: Water-motion receptors
structures.description: Sensory neurons trigger a startle when water moves nearby. Their connections reach the muscles and the beating hairs that propel the larva.
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

abilities.name: Steer toward a light
abilities.description: Illuminating one eyespot changed the beating of nearby swimming hairs. A simulation showed how that change steers the rotating larva toward light.

abilities.name: Dive under ultraviolet light
abilities.description: Larvae swam down when ultraviolet light came from all directions. Removing a light-sensitive protein abolished the response.

abilities.name: Startle when water vibrates
abilities.description: Vibration made larvae stop beating their swimming hairs and lift their paired side appendages. Mutants missing either of two sensory proteins failed to startle.

inherited.name: Nervous tissue inherited from an ancestor shared by bilaterians and cnidarians

nuances.claim: Every cell in the wiring dataset is a neuron.
nuances.reality: The volume contains muscles, glands and other cells alongside neurons. Many developing nerve cells had too few connections to classify.
nuances.evidence_quote: neuronal and non-neuronal cells

nuances.claim: A depth gauge has been demonstrated in the ocean.
nuances.reality: Experiments showed that the balance of blue and ultraviolet light controls swimming direction. The authors proposed that larvae could use this relationship to sense depth in the sea.
nuances.evidence_quote: may use it as a depth gauge

connectome.description: Serial electron microscopy reconstructed the whole-body network of a three-day-old larva. This describes the connected larval cells at that age.

stops.title: Echinoderms: seeing with a sea urchin

diverged_mya.value_basis: Midpoint of the published composite interval in Table 1. This is a branch split, not the age of the living species.

stops.summary: A long-spined sea urchin can move toward a broad dark shape and aim defensive spines toward an approaching shape. Experiments measured both responses. How the animal combines light signals across its body remains an open question.

structures.name: Radial nerves
structures.description: Five nerves follow the five sectors of the sea urchin body. Their role in guiding visually directed movement is a model prediction.
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

structures.name: Mouth nerve ring
structures.description: A ring around the mouth joins the radial nerves. A model proposes that activity from different directions meets here.
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

structures.name: Body-surface light sensors
structures.description: Tube feet are candidate sites for the light sensors. Much of the direct anatomical evidence comes from a different species, the purple sea urchin.
structures.evidence_quote: studies in the species Strongylocentrotus purpuratus
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

abilities.name: Approach a broad target
abilities.description: Urchins moved toward wide dark patterns even when the pattern and background had the same average brightness. The cells that direct the turn remain to be identified.

abilities.name: Aim defensive spines
abilities.description: A growing dark target on a screen caused urchins to aim spines toward it. Researchers measured the size needed to elicit a response. The responsible light sensors remain candidates.

inherited.name: Nervous tissue inherited from an ancestor shared by bilaterians and cnidarians

nuances.claim: A discrete eye is necessary to see a shape.
nuances.reality: These urchins distinguished broad patterns from a uniform background despite lacking eyes.
nuances.evidence_quote: discriminate spatial vision from phototaxis

nuances.reality: Li and colleagues built a model that reproduces orientation experiments. Its proposed connections still need anatomical tests.
nuances.evidence_quote: testable predictions

open_question.text: Which connections between the radial nerves and the nerve ring actually guide the animal toward a visual target?

stops.summary: An acorn worm has nerves spread under its skin, with a particularly dense network at the base of its snout. Two nerve cords run along its trunk. Different regions house different kinds of nerve cells.

structures.name: Snout nerve network
structures.description: The network is denser around the base of the snout. Its organization suggests a place where sensory information could come together.
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

structures.name: Back and belly nerve cords
structures.description: Gene markers reveal distinct sets of nerve cells in the two cords. Their different roles are still being worked out.
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

structures.name: Hatchling swimming band
structures.description: A ring of beating hairs near the rear of the hatchling drives it through the water.
structures.origin_scope: The source documents the anatomy. Its place of origin on the tree remains unresolved here.

abilities.name: Swim after hatching
abilities.description: Microscopy shows the band of beating hairs that propels hatchlings. The study did not identify a neural circuit that starts or stops swimming.

abilities.name: Adjust feeding to currents
abilities.description: In a flow tank, worms passed more sediment under moderate currents and less under strong currents. The experiment measured feeding through waste output. The responsible neurons are unknown.

nuances.claim: Does the collar cord share an origin with the chordate neural tube?

nuances.evidence_quote: may have had a diffuse nervous system

nuances.claim: A nerve net is uniform wherever you look.
nuances.reality: Microscopy found different cell types in different parts of the acorn worm. The network thickens around the snout base.
nuances.evidence_quote: regionalized structure
